Q: How do I get the 3D rotation from one orthogonal basis to another (quaternion or matrix) A:

The orthogonal & -normal base vectors that describe an orientation are the column vectors of a rotation matrix; i.e. the vectors r=right, u=up, f=forward they form a matrix

r_x u_x f_x
r_y u_y f_y
r_z u_z f_z

This matrix is the rotation matrix to get into that orientation.

So if you have two orientations R and R' then the transformation to get from R to R' is the compound transformation going from R to 𝟙 (identity) which is inv(R) followed by a rotation to R'. i.e.

T(R→R') = R' · inv(R)

Q: Pivoting table doesn't return the expected results A:

I dont know whether typo or not but you are pivoting on the wrong column. In your source, the team names (“Team 1"..“Team 4”) are in Team_name, while the thing you want to display (“Received”, “Risk”, XML strings) is in Value. Your current query pivots FOR Value, so SQL Server looks for columns named [Team 1], [Team 2] inside the Value column which will never match and everything becomes NULL.

You need to aggregate the Value and pivot on Team_name:


SELECT
    Attribute_displayname,
    [Team 1],
    [Team 2],
    [Team 3],
    [Team 4]
FROM (
    SELECT
        Attribute_displayname,
        Team_name,
        Value
    FROM #GenericTeam
) AS SRC
PIVOT (
    MAX(Value)              -- aggregate the Value
    FOR Team_name IN ([Team 1],[Team 2],[Team 3],[Team 4])
) AS p
ORDER BY Attribute_displayname;

You have lot of leading spaces in your [ Team 2], [ Team 3]. Kindly use [Team 2], [Team 3]. You can also do conditional aggregation:

SELECT
    Attribute_displayname,
    MAX(CASE WHEN Team_name = 'Team 1' THEN Value END) AS [Team 1],
    MAX(CASE WHEN Team_name = 'Team 2' THEN Value END) AS [Team 2],
    MAX(CASE WHEN Team_name = 'Team 3' THEN Value END) AS [Team 3],
    MAX(CASE WHEN Team_name = 'Team 4' THEN Value END) AS [Team 4]
FROM #GenericTeam
GROUP BY Attribute_displayname
ORDER BY Attribute_displayname;

If Value contains XML-like strings, ensure its stored as NVARCHAR(MAX) (or XML if truly XML). Mixing types can cause implicit conversions. Keep the bracketed identifiers consistent ([Team 2] not [ Team 2]). MAX(Value) will return NULL when all rows are NULL, which is expected for teams without a value.

Hope it gives you clarity.

Q: How to properly put/organize my unit tests inside my cargo binary project? A:

The idiom is to only compile the tests when you want to run them. You do this by annotating your module with:

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

See Test Organization in the Rust Book.
